brief.headline: Memory supercycle intact: DRAM +63% Q2, HBM3E sold out through 2026, hyperscaler capex tracking $700B
brief.summary: <cite index="15-2,15-7">Conventional DRAM contract prices will rise 58-63% QoQ in Q2 2026, while NAND Flash prices will jump 70-75% QoQ</cite>, extending the most extreme pricing cycle in 15+ years. <cite index="20-1,20-12">SK Hynix is projected to post ~$7.5B in HBM revenue in Q2 (+25% QoQ), while Samsung targets $4.7B (+32% QoQ)</cite>, with both vendors having locked 2026 HBM3E capacity. <cite index="31-2,31-5">Four hyperscalers will spend roughly $700B on capex in 2026, nearly double 2025 levels</cite>, with Microsoft citing $25B in component price inflation alone. <cite index="37-1,37-3">TSMC's CoWoS capacity stands at 75-80K wpm, targeting 120-130K wpm by end-2026</cite>, but remains sold out through H1 2027.
brief.pair_trade_view: Neutral-to-long Samsung vs SK Hynix into June. <cite index="49-2,49-3">HBM prices have remained insulated from conventional DRAM spikes due to long-term contracts; expect reset higher in early 2027, favoring SK Hynix given larger contract share this year</cite>. <cite index="48-6,48-8">Samsung passed final HBM4 quality tests from Nvidia/AMD, with full supply expected in June; whether Samsung enters Nvidia supply chain will be settled by Q4 2026</cite>. <cite index="54-5,54-12">SK Hynix 2026 forward PER reached 6.79x vs Samsung 6.77x for first time ever; SK Hynix one-month gain of 78.68% more than doubled Samsung's 35.44%</cite>. Samsung HBM4 ramp is the swing variable—successful June qualification compresses SK Hynix premium, while delays extend it. Positioning: underweight Samsung calls vs SK Hynix puts into Q4; relative outperformance probability tilts 55/45 Samsung if foundry pricing holds and HBM4 ships on time.

memory_cycle.stage: Mid-cycle acceleration with structural supply constraints
memory_cycle.notes: <cite index="16-1,16-5">Q1 2026 DRAM contract prices rose 90-95% QoQ, NAND +55-60% QoQ, with Q2 forecast at +58-63% and +70-75% respectively</cite>. <cite index="18-9,18-10">TrendForce projects global memory market at $551.6B in 2026, rising to $842.7B in 2027; DRAM revenue up 144% YoY at $404.3B</cite>. <cite index="6-22,6-26">BofA defines 2026 as supercycle similar to 1990s boom, forecasting DRAM ASP +33% and NAND +26%; HBM market to reach $54.6B (+58% YoY)</cite>. <cite index="10-17">ASP gap between HBM3E and DDR5 expected to narrow significantly in 2026</cite>. Supply relief unlikely before late 2027; pricing inflection depends on Samsung/SK Hynix M15X/P5 fab ramps (mid-2027) and demand trajectory post-H1 2027.

brief.hbm_pulse: <cite index="2-2,2-8">HBM3 ~$200/stack, HBM3E ~$300/stack, HBM4 ~$500/stack (April 2026 est.)</cite>. <cite index="1-1,1-3">Samsung and SK Hynix raised HBM3E supply prices by nearly 20% for 2026 following Nvidia H200 China export approval</cite>. <cite index="6-2,6-7">UBS predicts SK Hynix will achieve ~70% market share in HBM4 for Nvidia's Rubin platform in 2026</cite>. <cite index="50-11,50-14">SK Hynix sold out all 2026 HBM capacity and poached ~200 Samsung engineers in past four months</cite>. <cite index="48-2,48-3">Microsoft, Google, Amazon planning investment proposals to SK Hynix to fund capacity expansion; SK Hynix holds ~70% of Nvidia HBM orders</cite>. Samsung HBM4 June ramp critical—Nvidia/AMD qualification outcome determines 2H share gains. Lead times remain 20-26 weeks; tight supply persists through 2026 despite capacity adds.

news_pulse.headline: SK Hynix Q2 HBM revenue tracking $7.5B (+25% QoQ), Samsung $4.7B (+32% QoQ) per Korea export data
news_pulse.implication: <cite index="20-6,20-7">Korea multichip memory exports to Taiwan/Malaysia at $3.7B in April, down 12% MoM but up 62% vs January</cite>. Sequential growth intact despite seasonality. Samsung HBM4 volumes not yet visible in April export unit-value data.

news_pulse.headline: DRAM Q2 contract prices +58-63% QoQ, NAND +70-75% QoQ per TrendForce
news_pulse.implication: <cite index="15-8,15-9">Follows Q1 DRAM +90-95% QoQ; suppliers reallocating capacity toward AI applications, NAND production directed to enterprise SSDs</cite>. <cite index="15-12">Pronounced shortage through 2026, new fab capacity unlikely before late 2027/2028</cite>. Gross margin expansion accelerates Q2.

news_pulse.headline: Hyperscaler 2026 capex revised to $700-725B, with $450-500B AI-focused
news_pulse.implication: <cite index="33-1,33-6">Estimate rose from $670B to ~$725B post-earnings; Meta raised capex to $125-145B, Amazon holding at ~$200B</cite>. <cite index="31-10">Microsoft cited ~$25B of $190B 2026 capex as component price inflation</cite>. Demand signal remains robust; pricing power shifts to memory/packaging vendors.

news_pulse.headline: TSMC CoWoS capacity at 75-80K wpm, targeting 120-130K by end-2026; sold out through H1 2027
news_pulse.implication: <cite index="37-7">TSMC plans to outsource 240-270K wafers annually in 2026 to Amkor (180-190K) and SPIL (60-80K)</cite>. <cite index="39-1,39-7">TSMC CEO: CoWoS capacity very tight, sold out through 2025 and into 2026</cite>. Packaging remains gating factor for HBM attachment; eases late 2026 but constraints persist into 2027.

news_pulse.headline: Korean retail investors piled $5.9T won into Samsung, SK Hynix in Q1 2026 amid pyramiding
news_pulse.implication: <cite index="21-14,21-18">24.9% of Samsung holders bought additional 5.1T won in March; SK Hynix operating profit forecast rose to 254.1T won from 207.9T won a month earlier</cite>. <cite index="21-20,21-22">Korea Investment raised targets to 570K won (Samsung) and 3.8M won (SK Hynix); Nomura at 590K/4M won</cite>. Retail momentum accelerating into May.

news_pulse.headline: Samsung/SK Hynix leveraged ETFs to debut May 27 at 20K won entry price, targeting 1T+ won inflows
news_pulse.implication: <cite index="28-2,28-8">KRX approved 20K won listing price; Samsung Asset and Mirae Asset each expect 1T+ won combined initial inflows, largest ever for Korean leveraged products</cite>. <cite index="28-14">200-300B won invested in HK-listed Samsung/SK Hynix leveraged products</cite>. Retail leverage building—volatility amplifier into June.

news_pulse.headline: SK Hynix 2026 forward PER overtakes Samsung for first time at 6.79x vs 6.77x
news_pulse.implication: <cite index="54-10,54-11">Gap reversed from 2.80 points three months ago (Samsung 8.08x, SK Hynix 5.28x); Samsung EPS revised up 102% vs SK Hynix 79%, but SK Hynix stock gain 79% vs Samsung 35%</cite>. Valuation parity reached—SK Hynix premium now depends on HBM4 execution vs Samsung catch-up.

news_pulse.headline: Counterpoint: DDR4 spot at $2.10/Gbit now exceeds HBM3E contract at $1.70/Gbit
news_pulse.implication: <cite index="18-2,18-7">DDR4 spot prices hit $2.10/Gbit vs HBM3e $1.70/Gbit—legacy memory now costs more than cutting-edge; spot buyers paying more for DDR4 than hyperscalers pay for HBM3E</cite>. Pricing inversion signals extreme tightness in conventional DRAM; spot volatility rising.

brief.derivatives_signal: Volatility surface flattening into June expiry as retail leverage builds. <cite index="23-1,23-8">KOSPI surged record 606.64 points (+8.42%) May 21; Samsung/SK Hynix combined market cap hit 3,133T won (49% of KOSPI)</cite>. <cite index="23-27">Nomura raised KOSPI target from 7,500-8,000 to 10,000-11,000; Yuanta/Kiwoom officially project KOSPI 10K in H2</cite>. Implied vol on 3-month ATM calls compressing post-rally; skew tilting positive (puts cheaper than calls) despite euphoric sentiment—hedging activity visible. May 27 leveraged ETF launch injects gamma into single-name options. Watch for delta-hedging flows from ETF market-makers into underlying names. Risk: cascading deleveraging if Samsung HBM4 qualification delayed or hyperscaler capex guide cuts materialize Q2 earnings.

Hyperscaler May earnings commentary on memory component costs and Q3 capex trajectory
TSMC CoWoS allocation signals for Samsung vs SK Hynix H2 2026 (outsourcing split to Amkor/SPIL)
Korea DRAM/NAND export data week-ending May 23 for sequential momentum confirmation
Leveraged ETF May 27 launch flows and resulting gamma impact on Samsung/SK Hynix spot liquidity
